messages:
auto-incident-bot: PAGERS — GPU pool eu-west-1 -> saturation detected. queue_length=2140, avg_latency_tokens=620ms, autoscaler_errors=rate_limit/429 (x120 in 5m). Paging oncall.

alex (oncall): acked. joining. any immediate customer 5xx reports?

emily (support): we have ~18 open tickets referencing 503/timeout from eu region, some high-traffic tenants. Tickets started ~10:03 UTC.

sara (sre): looking at autoscaler logs now — seeing repeated scaleUp RPC failures: 429 from cloud provider + "quota reached" + also a handful of "instance launch timeout". autoscaler gave up after backoff.

kyle (infra): provider console shows quota at limit for that account: GPU quota consumed by other infra jobs + tonight's scheduled batch. raising a support case but slow.

miguel (runtime): runtime queues are piling; continuous batching prevents graceful shedding; tasks are hitting per-tenant throttles. We can temporarily reduce max_tokens for some models to reduce token throughput.

alex (oncall): quick mitigations list: 1) divert non-prod traffic out of eu-west-1 2) enable fallback to smaller quantized model for best-effort tenants 3) open emergency capacity with provider (if available) 4) shed low-priority jobs. who can run 1 & 2?

kyle (infra): I can cut non-prod routes now. running: `routingctl route disable --region eu-west-1 --tag=non-prod`

kyle (infra): done. non-prod traffic dropped ~11% of queued requests. see dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/cluster/eu-west-1-queue?orgId=1

miguel (runtime): implementing fallback config for tenants flagged best-effort. pushing policy change: switch model->redwood-small-quantized, max_tokens=256 for tag=best-effort.

miguel (runtime): policy pushed. expected token throughput reduction ~28%. queue_length dropping slightly.

sara (sre): autoscaler still failing on some scaleup attempts, but successful increments when we reduce target by 1. suggests provider rejecting larger instance types. logs: ```ERROR autoscaler.go:344 scaleUp failed: provider 429 quotaExceeded - attempted 8->12 gpus```

alex (oncall): can we do partial scale and re-balance across pools? maybe spin up new smaller pools in eu-central or use dedicated spare pools?

kyle (infra): spinning up a smaller aux pool in eu-west-2 (smaller instance SKU) as a fast fallback. if provider quota is per-region, this will help. kickoff: `infra create-pool --region eu-west-2 --sku g4dn-small --count 6 --tags=aux-fallback`

kyle (infra): aux pool creation in progress. might take ~6-8 min.

tara (cs): heads-up to CS: impacted tenants include Acme Corp (high traffic), BetaApps (~degraded), and a couple of long-tail customers. I'm drafting inbound message and prioritizing ACME ticket.

emily (support): mounting support queue. tagging ACME as P1, adding mitigation notes: route change + fallback model.

zack (eng-ml): small-quantized outputs are slightly noisier — will call that out to CS so expectations are clear. adding eval note: fallback might change hallucination profile.

miguel (runtime): aux pool is healthy and new workers registering. starting job drain & cross-region routing: `routingctl route add --from eu-west-1 --to eu-west-2 --percent 20 --selector=best-effort||aux-route`

miguel (runtime): cross-region routing applied. traffic shifting ~18%. queue load in eu-west-1 reduced and latency improving.

sara (sre): monitoring autoscaler — some success now with partial scale and rebalanced traffic. queue_length 2140 -> 980 over 12 minutes. customer errors dropping.

alex (oncall): status check: any remaining 5xx spikes?

emily (support): ACME still seeing intermittent 503s but severity reduced. BetaApps stable. pile of low-priority requests still delayed but not failing.

kyle (infra): provider support responded: quote -> "quota is at account-level due to scheduled batch jobs, we can temporarily raise limit but need ticket approval (ETA 45min)." I've requested expedite.

alex (oncall): good. next: runbook items for postmortem: - document cause (quota + autoscaler retry/backoff assumptions) - action items (quota visibility, pre-warming, autoscaler resilience) - customer communication thread. assign owners.

sara (sre): assigned: sara -> postmortem writeup, kyle -> quota visibility + provider escalation notes, miguel -> runtime graceful-shedding + fallback policy audit, zack -> eval impact on outputs, tara/emily -> customer comms.

miguel (runtime): quick note for postmortem: autoscaler currently treats 429 as fatal for that attempt and increases backoff exponentially; propose to treat transient 429 as retryable with jittered backoff and attempt smaller increments when 429 observed.

sara (sre): agreed. also propose new alert: `queue_length > 1000 && scale_attempts_failed > 3` to page infra earlier. current alert threshold was >2000 which was too late.

kyle (infra): action: add visibility to provider quotas in our console (per-account/per-region), and add pre-approval flow to request emergency quota bumps from provider partners. owner=kyle.

zack (eng-ml): action: add a fallback model contract that includes evaluation artifacts and a deterministic flag so CS can opt-in/opt-out per-customer. owner=zack.

tara (cs): action: customer-facing post explaining temporary fallback behavior + ETA for full restoration. owner=tara.

emily (support): action: backlog triage plan and script for status updates to affected customers. owner=emily.

alex (oncall): immediate follow-ups: 1) keep aux pool + cross-region routing until provider quota confirmed 2) monitor error rate for 1hr, then demobilize.

miguel (runtime): agreed. set retention: keep aux pool up 2 hours after error-rate <0.5% sustained for 15m.

sara (sre): closing incident channel in ~30m once errors stable. creating postmortem ticket and linking this thread.

alex (oncall): thanks all. great triage. :thumbsup:

auto-incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (provisional) — error rate returned to baseline, queue length stabilized under threshold. postmortem ticket: PM-2147.

sara (sre): Postmortem quick notes to include in ticket: timeline, root cause (quota exhaustion + autoscaler treating 429 as hard fail), mitigations applied (non-prod cut, fallback model, aux pool, cross-region routing), customer impact summary, action items & owners.

kyle (infra): I'll add provider ticket ID and follow-up notes once support reply finalized.

zack (eng-ml): will run regression eval for fallback model and share results in the postmortem doc.

emily (support): I'll follow up with status messages sent to affected customers and paste templates in the PM ticket.

miguel (runtime): action item: implement smaller increment scaling mode + 429 retry policy. ETA for change: within 2 sprints. owner=miguel.

sara (sre): action item: lower alert threshold and add synthetic traffic monitor for queue backpressure. ETA: next week. owner=sara.

alex (oncall): closing notes: good coordination, kept customer impact limited. we'll reconvene in the postmortem write-up.
